issue: Deep review defaults to 180 days with refresh 30 days before expiry for every registry charity, independent of whether any grant is pending.
recurring_work_created: ~2.43 scheduled renewals per active recipient-year (365/150). At 4 grants per recipient and 9 grants per account this is ~5.5 renewals per account-year; with human deep review (15 min) ~82 min/account-year, more than the whole 48-minute allowance.
proposed_change: Define 'deep review' as automated evidence refresh with human review only when evidence changed, conflicts or is missing; renew lazily (only recipients with pending or scheduled grants, or when a grant arrives after expiry); keep approval- and release-time status checks and event-triggered invalidation unchanged.
safety_constraints: Transaction-time checks at approval and release remain mandatory; fail safe when stale; sponsor may tighten; nonstandard classes (foreign, ER, Type I/II SO, fiscal sponsors, churches without listing) keep scheduled human review; independent sampling of automated renewals; record source posting dates.

issue: Pre-contracted December surge reviewers and independent reconsideration reviewers must be exclusive to one sponsor; combined with the December readiness gate this forces a per-sponsor surge bench that a multi-sponsor servicer cannot pool.
recurring_work_created: A standby bench per sponsor every December (activation, training, conflict attestation, roster upkeep) - step-fixed cost per sponsor rather than per unit of work; TEV-003 already shows per-sponsor floors dominate the administrator model.
proposed_change: Keep exclusivity for persons exercising A3+ reserved authority; allow pooled, non-deciding preparation staff (evidence packets, outreach, data repair) across sponsors under tenant isolation and conflict attestation; allow a shared pre-qualified surge pool from which each sponsor appoints named reviewers for a fixed window, with no concurrent appointment.
safety_constraints: No person decides for two sponsors concurrently; tenant isolation (CNV-ARC-002); conflict attestations; SoD unchanged; access revoked before reassignment.

issue: Human false-positive sanctions dispositions expire after 12 months even when subject attributes and list entries are unchanged.
recurring_work_created: Annual re-disposition of the same false positives for recurring grantees and long-lived donors.
proposed_change: Expire reuse on change events (subject attribute, list entry, new matching entry, officer authority) and replace the fixed 12-month expiry with a sampled periodic re-validation (e.g. 10% of reused dispositions per year) chosen by the compliance officer.
safety_constraints: Every list update still delta-screens; any new or changed entry re-triggers; screening before each release unchanged; true matches never auto-cleared; no cross-sponsor reuse for donors/advisors.

issue: Tier-2 triggers (governmental unit, Type I/II supporting organisation, fiscally sponsored project, grant large relative to recipient revenue) fire on every repeat grant to the same recipient and purpose class.
recurring_work_created: Repeat enhanced reviews of recipients already determined; replay shows 64-72% of exception rows are repeat recipients.
proposed_change: Allow a Tier-2 determination to be reused for the same recipient, sponsor and purpose class within its freshness window unless a material fact changes (amount band, restriction, affiliation signal, status), with reuse visible in the decision record and sampled by the CNV-GRT-011 programme.
safety_constraints: Donor/advisor affiliation and benefit signals always re-trigger; reuse never crosses sponsors as a decision (facts only, per CNV-GRT-004); sampling increases after errors.

issue: Each new source starts in ProvisionalCalibration with exact match only and 100% human review for a full close cycle; on a multi-sponsor servicer the same bank or custodian file format is recalibrated per sponsor tenant.
recurring_work_created: One full close cycle of 100% review per sponsor per feed at every onboarding (step-fixed onboarding hours).
proposed_change: Permit a feed format calibrated and approved for one tenant to start new tenants at that format's approved tolerances, with a shortened parallel run (e.g. 10 business days) and per-sponsor controller approval.
safety_constraints: Per-sponsor controller still signs off; exact-match-only fallback on any unexplained break; tolerance evidence from the reference tenant must not expose that tenant's data.

issue: Quarterly board report sampling (CNV-GOV-008) and decision-quality sampling (CNV-GRT-011) are specified separately and could be run as two sampling programmes.
recurring_work_created: Duplicate sample selection and review each quarter per sponsor.
proposed_change: State that one risk-stratified, error-bound sample satisfies both clauses when sized to the stricter requirement.
safety_constraints: Sample size never below either clause's requirement; qualified independent reviewers; increase after material errors.

issue: Without a recorded board delegation the operating model is individual accountable batch decisions on AI-prepared dossiers for every grant.
recurring_work_created: Sponsor-retained minutes on every routine grant (~0.3-0.5 min each, ~3-5 min/account-year for a typical account) and slower turnaround; the servicer cannot reach its redesigned cost until delegation exists.
proposed_change: Make a model delegation resolution, policy-version evidence pack and board-report template part of sponsor onboarding so delegation can be adopted at go-live; measure time-to-delegation as an onboarding KPI.
safety_constraints: Board decides; delegation expires within 12 months; exceptions remain with named officers; no change to s4966(d)(3) fund-manager recording.

issue: Checks remain a first-class rail: daily positive pay, 90-day void, no automatic re-credit; each stale or returned check becomes a manual case.
recurring_work_created: Check grants cost ~$4 and ~3-4 min including returns vs ~$0.30 and ~0.1 min for EFT; Fidelity still pays 33% of grants by check.
proposed_change: Add an EFT-by-default policy option: checks only on charity or donor request or where no verified EFT destination exists; automated outreach to enrol recipients at first check; reissue to verified EFT destination where enrolled.
safety_constraints: Destination evidence rules (bank-originated match or document + independent callback) unchanged; duplicate-payment controls on reissue; unclaimed-property law respected; accessible fallback for charities without bank enrolment.

issue: Delegated customer roles expire on events with risk-based recertification, and affiliation attestations need periodic confirmation; cadence is unspecified.
recurring_work_created: Donor/advisor contacts and chasing for periodic confirmations across all funds, including inactive ones (~20% of accounts).
proposed_change: Default periodic confirmation to annual, bundled with the annual statement, only for funds with active advisors or affiliation-sensitive grants; event-driven triggers carry the safety load.
safety_constraints: Stale mandatory attestation still blocks affected decisions; event triggers (advisor change, affiliation signal) unchanged.
